liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Black Peter** (3 reviews): Garcia spiked the mic after the last verse of Black Peter; Garcia croaked through Black Peter with no voice [11][13][16]
- **Promised Land** (2 reviews): Promised Land going into Greatest Story Ever Told was a very rare pairing; The Promised Land into Greatest Story Ever Told opener was interesting despite Garcia's missing voice [8][14]
- **Gimme Some Lovin'** (2 other sources): Garcia teases The Wheel just before Gimme Some Lovin'; Garcia teases The Wheel before Gimme Some Lovin' [1][4]
- **Althea** (1 review): With Garcia lacking a voice, Althea nearly lost its bearing [18]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Brent sang lead on Little Red Rooster, and the solo was strong [8]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): Garcia croaked through Crazy Fingers with no voice; reviewer thought Weir should have led the second set [13]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Lovelight was a nice surprise [12]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-04-03.153797.cmc4-mk41.oade-bryant-gastwirt.miller.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 18 songs; 139 min [1]
- **gd1988-04-03.sbd.miller.91161.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 129 min; rated 2.89/5 by 9 [2]
- **gd88-04-03.sbd.painoman.9628.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 127 min; rated 2.22/5 by 18 [3]
- **gd1988-04-03.154410.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 129 min [4]

## Around the show

- Campers filled the ground in front of the state capital building, whippet canisters scattered about, with bad weather all three days [8]
- Reviewer attended after the Meadowlands run, skipping its last night, and found Garcia's voice horrible [9]
- Garcia's voice gave out and he angrily threw down the mic [10]
- It was Easter Sunday, and the show went ahead because cancelling was out of the question [10]
- Garcia's voice was completely shot, but he pushed through the show anyway [11]
- Phil tried singing, and freaky hippies in the aisle forced the reviewer to stand all show [12]
- Reviewer attended nights two and three and heard reports of Garcia throwing the mic [14]
- Reviewer and two friends attended and thought they were having a bad trip; Garcia shouldn't have sung after Crazy Fingers [16]
- Reviewer found it weak and perfunctory after the great Hampton run, and sold tickets for the rest of the tour [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-04-03.153797.cmc4-mk41.oade-bryant-gastwirt.miller.flac1644**: taped by From the DAT collection of Rich Gastwirt; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  October 6, 2021; source: (FOB) Schoeps CMC4/MK41 (Oade Brothers) > PCM Master (Robert Bryant) > DAT (44.1k) [1]
- **gd1988-04-03.sbd.miller.91161.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) D [2]. Also: Unknown mics to cassette master to DAT to CD; A short patch in Gimme Some Lovin' came from a source labeled soundboard but actually an audience recording [2]
- **gd88-04-03.sbd.painoman.9628.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>?>CD (Possible Matrix) [3]. Also: Soundboard to CD, possibly a matrix, via Ankh-af-na-khonsu and seeded to etree by PainoMan [3]
- **gd1988-04-03.154410.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  October 6, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90) [4]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; multiple masters were combined to complete the show [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1988-04-03 Hartford Civic Center, Hartford, CT, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1988-04-03-hartford-civic-center-hartford-ct-usa/) [21]
